solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Periodic table of a sort

blocks.note: first meaning: happening now and then
second meaning: a small side table moved about as needed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodic table' looks like the chemistry chart, but the clue splits after 'Periodic': an occasional table is a small piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that recurs at intervals rather than constantly is occasional, and an occasional table is a light side table.

clue.text: Individual cops caught in the past

indicators.note: to cop is to catch hold of, so the individual grabs the next letter inside it

blocks.note: one individual
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lone police officer arrested someone long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cops' looks like a noun for police but is the verb meaning grabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some former time, which is in the past.

clue.text: I must stop talk about one branching out

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the letter goes inside like a stopper

blocks.note: to confer is to talk something over
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insisting on cutting short a discussion about a person diversifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branching out' suggests expanding a business; read literally it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree, which literally grows branches.

clue.text: It's a job to make posh satanists change

indicators.note: to change is to alter, so these letters take a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A daunting task: converting upper-class devil-worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving customers in a store is a paid occupation, so it is a job.

clue.text: Look, a ham must be ordered, OK

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh sequence, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a deli counter insisting a ham be ordered, all right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'OK' looks like a casual 'all right' but is the US postal code for the state.
explanation.definitionFit: OK is the official two-letter postal abbreviation of the American state.

clue.text: I pretend to put in air-con right

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the little word goes inside the others

blocks.note: AC is short for air conditioning
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone faking having installed the air conditioning correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: an actor could say 'I pretend' of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's job is to feign being someone else, so one might describe the work as pretending.

clue.text: Drinks knocked back can make one this

definitions.text: Drinks knocked back can make one this

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but read literally the word is turned backwards

blocks.note: nips are small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: A warning that downing too many drinks leaves your head whirling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: reverse NIPS to get SPIN, which is what too many drinks make your head do.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking makes a person dizzy, so their head seems to whirl round, which is to spin.

clue.text: One promising book prefaced by head of Penguin

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the publisher's name
prefaced means preceded, so the selected letter comes in front of the book

blocks.note: the first letter of Penguin
a ledger is an account book

explanation.surface: A promising novel introduced by the boss of the publisher Penguin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledger is someone who makes a pledge, a solemn promise.

clue.text: Books written in Chinese, possibly about special symbols

indicators.note: words written in something sit inside it, so the books go within the next word

blocks.note: a Chinese person is an example of a national of a country
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Books composed in Chinese characters, perhaps concerning special symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Notational means relating to notation, a system of written signs as in music or mathematics.

clue.text: Tory party's flat, according to Trump

blocks.note: Con is the short form of Conservative
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A jibe that a Conservative party's policy is as flat as Trump says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to Trump' just marks the word as American: Trump made his name in property, and a condo is the US word for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Condo, short for condominium, is the American term for an apartment owned within a larger block.

clue.text: Yellowish teeth may be repaired with this kind of lead

blocks.clueFragment: teeth may be repaired with this
blocks.note: lute is a sealing cement; dentists use luting cement to fix crowns
a scent is a trail or lead followed by a hound or detective

explanation.surface: Stained teeth being fixed with some sort of lead filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the metal, but here it is a trail to follow, as in 'on the scent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutescent is a botanical term for something tending towards a yellow colour.

clue.text: Cryptograms confused a posh gangster

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so these letters are jumbled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coded messages that baffled an upper-class mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Steganographs are messages concealed within other material, a form of secret writing akin to cryptograms.

clue.text: One taking a slug, but only a little one?

definitions.text: One taking a slug, but only a little one?

blocks.clueFragment: One taking a slug, but only a little one?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone eating or swallowing a small garden slug, or a small drink
setter's reading: a slug is a punch, so this is a boxer in one of the lightest weight divisions

explanation.walkthrough: A slug is a hard punch; the 'little one' is the boxer's small size, not a small mollusc or a sip of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a boxing division for light fighters, so such a boxer takes punches from opponents of modest size.

clue.text: Socialist leader: bald and without accent?

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of Socialist is used

blocks.note: the first letter of Socialist
having no tresses, no locks of hair

explanation.surface: A hairless left-wing leader who speaks with no regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accent' suggests a way of speaking; here it means stress on a syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is the emphasis or accent on a syllable, so something stressless has no accent.

clue.text: Boring book about passion ultimately sucks

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the following word is used
about means surrounding, so the volume wraps round what follows

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger, a passion
the last letter of sucks

explanation.surface: A dull read in which romance ends up being rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passion' suggests romance, but here it is anger; 'about' puts the volume round both the anger and the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boring is tedious and wearying, which is what tiresome means.

clue.text: Possible local port for Spanish district

blocks.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, and a bar may be one
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port city

explanation.surface: Looking for a nearby glass of port in a Spanish neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the wine served at the local; it is Rio. In Britain 'the local' is the nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrio is the Spanish word for a neighbourhood or quarter of a town.

clue.text: A dissolute guy hugged by favourite flapper

indicators.note: something hugged is enclosed in arms, so it goes inside the next word

blocks.note: a teacher's pet is the favourite
taken as written
a rake is a man of loose morals

explanation.surface: A debauched man embraced by his favourite 1920s good-time girl.
explanation.walkthrough: A flapper is a 1920s young woman, which fits the rake; here it is literally something that flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot, a bird that flaps its wings in flight.

clue.text: Still square and homosocial essentially

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core, so only the central letters of the next word count

blocks.note: square as in all square, level
the two central letters of homosocial

explanation.surface: Describing someone as staid and keen on same-sex friendships.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so and still both mean nevertheless, conceding a point while maintaining another.

clue.text: Caps former top players picked up

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: ex means former, and seeds are top-ranked players in a tennis draw

explanation.surface: Ex-internationals selected to win more caps for their country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caps' suggests international appearances in sport, but it is the verb meaning surpasses.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap something is to outdo or top it, which is what exceeding means.

clue.text: Old queen enthralled by country view

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
R for Regina, Latin for queen
the Central American country

explanation.surface: A former monarch captivated by a rural landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping view of a landscape.

clue.text: You might say one is the thing

definitions.note: cryptic: 'a', the word you might say for one, is an example

blocks.note: first meaning: the word 'a', which you say for one, belongs to this part of speech
second meaning: an item or object

explanation.surface: Someone declaring that a particular item is just what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' (meaning one) and 'the' are both grammatical articles, so the linking 'the' is itself an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the part of speech covering 'a' and 'the' and also any particular object or item.

clue.text: Really gutted to be suffering bird flu?

blocks.note: first meaning: the British idiom for bitterly disappointed
second meaning, taken literally: a pet bird that is unwell

explanation.surface: Someone devastated at having caught avian influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick as a parrot' is a British footballing cliché for deep disappointment; read literally it is a bird that is ill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes extreme dismay, the state of being gutted, while literally picturing an unwell parrot.

clue.text: Mail perhaps dismissing top Republican's affair

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: chain mail is a kind of armour
the first R, for Republican, is the top one

explanation.surface: A tabloid like the Mail exposing a leading Republican's love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like the British tabloid the Daily Mail; it is chain mail. Of the two Rs in the armour, the top (first) one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, especially a secret one.

clue.text: Duty paid for by this paper?

blocks.note: as in 'the drinks are on me'
the newspaper speaking of itself as we, us

explanation.surface: A tax or levy that the newspaper itself is footing the bill for.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden of obligation, a duty or responsibility.

clue.text: Choose baton with European conductor

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
a baton is a short rod
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Picking the baton for a continental orchestra conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' with baton paints an orchestra; the definition is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal that conducts electricity into or out of a circuit or cell.

clue.text: Nut training around end of autumn

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the season word

blocks.note: PE is physical education
ca is circa, Latin for around
the final letter of autumn

explanation.surface: A squirrel getting ready to store nuts as autumn ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is the nut of a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: Band seen hanging around Miss World?

blocks.note: first meaning: a long strip of cloth
second meaning: what a pageant winner wears draped across one shoulder

explanation.surface: A pop group loitering near a beauty queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The music group is the false scent; the band is a ribbon of fabric worn across the body by contestants.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty contestants wear a long strip of cloth over one shoulder bearing their title.

clue.text: We might be at a March exam in new radical prose

definitions.text: We might be at a March

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order
in means placed inside, so the test sits within the remade letters

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for radical
taken as written
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Students sitting a March exam on newly radical writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M dresses the definition up as the month; it is a demonstration march.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrators who take to the streets in a march are protesters.
